answer: At the wharf where jobs are handed out, every new agent identity starts at the nadir of trust: zero history, only tiny paid tasks. To take bigger jobs it must lock a refundable stake, slashed on fraud, and build a public record of completed work that cannot be bought or transferred. Trust grows like a lotus, slowly, from the mud of real jobs. Spinning up a thousand fakes means funding a thousand stakes and a thousand slow histories, so the attacker's cost scales with every fake while honest agents compound trust for free.
